# What `lib/app.g.dart` contains

As of v0.4.0 (`cli/templates/app.g.dart.jinja`). One plain go_router plus
Riverpod file, meant to be read and committed. It never names your types
except for a typed `extra` and enum segments or query parameters, which it
imports by name (`import '...' show Category;`). Everything else flows through
inference.

## The header

```text
// GENERATED by fespalier from lib/app/. Do not edit; run `fsp gen`.
// ignore_for_file: type=lint, unused_import, unused_element
//
//   /           HomeRoute   page.dart  (layout, transition)
//   /items/:id  ItemRoute   items/$id/page.dart  (data, transition)
```

The route table in the comment is what `fsp routes` prints. Files are imported
as `_i0`, `_i1`, ...; a `$` in a path is escaped (`items/\$id/page.dart`).

## `AppRoutes`

| Member                                                                   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `router({initialLocation, observers, restorationScopeId, navigatorKey})` | A whole `GoRouter` for `MaterialApp.router(routerConfig:)`. Passes `extraCodec:` when `extra_codec.dart` exists, and `errorBuilder` shows `notFound(uri)`. **No `refreshListenable`** |
| `mount({at = '/', navigatorKey})`                                        | The routes alone (`List<RouteBase>`), to put inside your own `GoRouter`                                                                                                               |
| `base`                                                                   | Where the tree is mounted: `'/'`, or the `at` given to `mount`. Typed routes read it, so `.location` stays right under a prefix                                                       |
| `rootNavigatorKey`                                                       | The root navigator's `GlobalKey<NavigatorState>`: the one you supplied, else its own                                                                                                  |
| `notFound(uri)`                                                          | The nearest `not_found.dart` to `uri` (what `errorBuilder` calls)                                                                                                                     |
| `matchUrl(uri)` / `dataAt(uri)`                                          | A `UrlMatch?` / the data providers, outermost first. No guard runs, no widget is built. `null`: no route, or a segment did not parse                                                  |
| `all`, `byType`, `byPath`, `match(uri)`                                  | Forwarded from `AppManifest` (see below)                                                                                                                                              |

`mount` **stores** `at` and `navigatorKey` in static fields, so the last call
wins. `router()` calls `mount()` itself.

## `AppManifest`

`all` (a `const` list of `RouteInfo`, in route-table order), `byType` (typed
route class to info), `byPath` (path template to info), `of(GoRouterState)` (the
route a layout is showing; `null` in a not-found view) and `match(uri)`. With
`output_manifest:` it lives in its own library (`AppRoutes.all`, `byType`,
`byPath`, `match` then exist only if the manifest is in `app.g.dart`; import the
manifest library and use `AppManifest` instead, which has the same name in both
modes). `AppRoutes.matchUrl` and `dataAt` always stay in `app.g.dart`.

## Typed routes

Every page and redirect gets a `final class XRoute extends TypedLocation` with a
`const` constructor taking its segments (required) and query parameters
(optional):

```dart
ProductRoute(id: 42).go(context);
const SearchRoute(q: 'ap', page: 2).location;   // /search?q=ap&page=2
```

- `location`: the full location, mount prefix included, canonical spelling; nulls
  and empty lists are left out of the query.
- `locationFor(locale)`, and `locale:` on `go`, `push<T>` and `replace`:
  localized spellings (see `fespalier-routing`).
- `static of(context)` and `static maybeOf(context)` (since 0.5.0): the route at
  the location the widget belongs to, parsed by `AppRoutes.matchUrl`; and, for a
  route with segments or query parameters, `copyWith`, a getter whose type is a
  function with the fields' types (a private `_keep` sentinel behind it tells
  null from omitted). See `fespalier-routing`.
- A route with a typed `extra` has `go`, `push` and `replace` overrides taking
  `extra:`.
- A route with a `data.dart` also has: `static data` (the provider; a family
  when it has keys), `static watch(ref, {keys})`, `static read(ref, {keys})`,
  an **instance** `prefetch(ref, {keepFor})` and an **instance**
  `refresh(ref)`. `watch` and `read` are static on purpose (see
  `fespalier-data`).
- A section's `data.dart` gets `<Folder>Section` with the same five members, all
  static (`fespalier-data`).

## Generated providers

A `data()` function becomes `FutureProvider.autoDispose.family(...)` (or
`StreamProvider`). With `data_retry: none` it carries
`retry: (retryCount, error) => null`; with the default `inherit` it sets no
policy, so the app's `ProviderScope(retry:)` applies. A `data.dart` that
exports its own provider (`final data = ...`) or selects one is used as is.

## What the file does not do

- No `redirect` on a `ShellRoute` or `StatefulShellRoute`; guards hang on each
  page's `GoRoute`, and go_router runs a matched route's redirect for deep links
  and navigation inside shells, tabs included.
- A segment that does not parse shows `not_found.dart` and skips the guards that
  read segments or query parameters; a guard that takes neither still runs first.
- Static routes are sorted before dynamic ones before catch-alls at each level,
  so go_router's first match is the most specific.
